title: Mool Chand Kushwaha v. State of U.P. and others
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Yatindra Singh, J.; Kashi Nath Pandey, J.
headnote: A consumer's writ challenging a theft-assessment Recovery Certificate as issued without complying with the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is dismissed for default when none appears for the petitioner on the revised list. An earlier conditional stay of recovery is overtaken by the dismissal.
facts: Mool Chand Kushwaha challenged a Recovery Certificate dated 25 November 2009 sent by the distribution licensee to the Collector, Jhansi, seeking Rs 28,185 plus notice charges for alleged theft of electricity found on a check of his premises on 29 November 2008. He alleged non-compliance with mandatory requirements of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. On 28 April 2011 recovery was stayed till the next date if he deposited Rs 15,000 within four weeks without prejudice. On 20 July 2011 none appeared for him.

holding_units.holding: The writ petition is dismissed for default, no one being present for the petitioner when the list was revised.

not_decided.point: Whether the Recovery Certificate dated 25.11.2009 for the alleged theft assessment was issued without complying with the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005
not_decided.note: Dismissed for default; the Supply Code challenge and the theft assessment were not examined on merits.
